newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota governor proposes $1.94 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota governor proposes $1.94 billion budget.

text.p: North Dakota Gov. Ed Schafer unveiled a $1.94 general fund budget for the 1997-99 bienium Thursday that includes increased funding for education and water development.
Schafer's proposed spending plan allocated $40 million more for primary and secondary education, $35 million for higher education and $5 million for water development.
In his budget speech before the legislature, Schafer said that lawmakers have $147 million in new revenues available due to economic growth.

"Our economic growth enables us to provide not necessarily more, but better government service for the health, safety and education of our people," the governor said. "As careful stewards of this hard-earned revenue, we will fund necessary and essential state programs carefully and make additional wise investments that will provide ongoing returns to our state."

If revenues exceed the $147 million projection, Schafer proposed setting excess oil and gas tax funds aside in a natural resources trust fund, while using the remainder of the excess funds for water development projects and provide taxpayer refunds.
Schafer also addressed the issue of equity in school funding, noting that the state supreme court in 1994 narrowly upheld the constitutionality of the current funding system.

He called on lawmakers to "settle the equity issue this session and give all our children equal access to excellence and quality." He added that his proposed budget includes $20 million for legislative efforts to improve the school funding system.
North Dakota's fiscal year begins July 1.
